answer: Random jury of 9 drawn per challenge without replacement. An attacker holding k fraction of identities wins a full jury only k^9 of the time — 10% ownership yields 10^-9 odds. Each sybil must maintain independent stake and uptime across the entire voyage of epochs, not just one sonnet-like burst. This bridge between identity cost and sampling probability means honest majority always settles verdicts; farming collapses because expected payoff scales with k^9 while costs scale with k. Works because exponential sampling dilution makes marginal sybils strictly value-destroying.
